rows.final_action: SUBMIT: Amazon MTurk annotators compared generated responses pairwise, with responses randomly shuffled to hide model identity. The criteria were Plausibility (whether a response fits its context) and Content Richness (whether it is diverse and informative). CITATIONS: ["qasper_2001_05467"]

SUBMIT: No rank relative to other teams is given in the inspected results and conclusion. Human evaluation was not yet available at writing time, and the reported comparisons among the authors' own approaches do not establish a challenge ranking. CITATIONS: ["qasper_1909_00542"]

SUBMIT: The paper uses four evaluation metrics: (1) Exact Match (EM) — 1 if the predicted plan matches the ground truth plan exactly, else 0; (2) F1 score — the harmonic average of precision and recall over the test set; (3) Edit Distance — the minimum number of insertions, deletions, or swaps needed to turn the predicted behavior sequence into the ground truth sequence; and (4) Goal Match (GM) — 1 if the predicted plan reaches the correct final destination, even if the full sequence doesn't match exactly, else 0. CITATIONS: ["qasper_1810_00663"]

SUBMIT: The system's performance is measured in two complementary ways. Quantitatively, the visual-question-generation model is evaluated with the BLEU metric on a validation set (achieving a BLEU score of 2.07), while the dialogue/feedback generation quality is assessed via manual (human) evaluation of grammatical correctness and content appropriateness. Additionally, a usability study was conducted with real users (with and without mild cognitive impairment): after 30-minute sessions, participants completed a five-point Likert survey rating how much they liked the system, how engaging it was, and how difficult it was, yielding average scores of 4.6 (amusing/engaging) and 2.6 (difficulty). CITATIONS: ["qasper_1910_11949"]
SUBMIT: The paper reports about 10,700 training examples after sampling. CITATIONS: ["qasper_1907_01413"]
SUBMIT: No BERT component is described in the inspected architecture. It uses GloVe, ELMo, and character-level LSTM embeddings. CITATIONS: ["qasper_1810_01570"]
SUBMIT: BERT was pre-trained on Wikipedia and BooksCorpus. CITATIONS: ["qasper_1909_07512"]

SUBMIT: The paper reports 25 participating teams and a range of neural-network models, but its detailed approach summary covers nine workshop submissions. That evidence does not establish whether every one of the 25 teams used a neural network. CITATIONS: ["qasper_2002_01359"]

SUBMIT: The retrieved text discusses comparisons with existing LibriSpeech systems and points to result tables, but it does not provide a recoverable previous-best accuracy value in these passages. I cannot supply that number from the available evidence. CITATIONS: ["qasper_2002_02562"]

SUBMIT: The baseline search returned no matches. The model-comparison passages describe the proposed architectures but do not identify a baseline system, so I cannot name one from this evidence. CITATIONS: ["qasper_1910_05608"]

SUBMIT: Yes. When compared in isolation without ELMo, language modeling performs best, followed by MNLI; most remaining pretraining tasks perform near the random baseline. Different target tasks benefit from different forms of pretraining. CITATIONS: ["qasper_1812_10860"]

SUBMIT: The retrieved passages identify the Recipes and ProPara datasets but do not specify their language coverage. I cannot confirm from these passages whether the reported evaluations are English-only. CITATIONS: ["qasper_1909_02635"]

SUBMIT: Monotonicity reasoning is inference by replacing words while accounting for the interaction between lexical meaning and syntactic structure. It includes upward and downward reasoning. CITATIONS: ["qasper_1906_06448"]

SUBMIT: The paper describes prior state-of-the-art multi-source transformer APE systems from WMT 2018: pal-EtAl:2018:WMT used three self-attention-based encoders, including a joint encoder over source and MT; tebbifakhr-EtAl:2018:WMT won the NMT subtask using sequence-level losses; shin-lee:2018:WMT used separate encoders with additional source-to-MT and source-to-post-edit attention. The PBSMT-subtask winner used two encoders and stacked source-to-post-edit cross-attention above MT-to-post-edit cross-attention. CITATIONS: ["qasper_1908_06151"]
SUBMIT: The ICSI meeting corpus is comprised of 75 meetings and about 70 hours of real-time audio duration. CITATIONS: ["qasper_1910_10869"]

SUBMIT: The paper describes a hand-curated resource of complete inflection tables for 198 lemmata, tagged using UniMorph. The inspected resource description does not explain how the underlying forms were originally collected or elicited, so that collection procedure remains unclear. CITATIONS: ["qasper_2004_02083"]

SUBMIT: They collected their own Russian-language Twitter corpus through the Streaming API filter endpoint, using a heuristic query of Russian function words such as conjunctions, pronouns and prepositions. CITATIONS: ["qasper_1602_08741"]
SUBMIT: The experiments use WMT18 English-German, WMT16 English-Romanian, and WMT15 English-French bitext. WMT Newscrawl supplies the monolingual data. CITATIONS: ["qasper_1906_06442"]

SUBMIT: Yes, they report qualitative manual inspection of generated definitions and examples. The inspected passage supports that claim, without establishing a separate scored human-evaluation study. CITATIONS: ["qasper_1905_06512"]

SUBMIT: The inspected setup describes image captioning experiments on COCO using the Karpathy split. It does not name a separate reinforcement-learning environment, so I cannot supply that name from these passages. CITATIONS: ["qasper_2003_09971"]

SUBMIT: One retrieved database description covers 42 languages. That is an example of the evaluated scale, not a demonstrated upper limit; the retrieved conclusion gives no numerical capacity limit, so I cannot establish the maximum language-set size. CITATIONS: ["qasper_2001_11899"]

SUBMIT: The inspected passages describe the topic-detection method as a baseline for a future extensive analysis of how people engage in Twitter threads across news types. They do not report engagement findings, so I cannot answer that comparison from this evidence. CITATIONS: ["qasper_1911_08370"]

SUBMIT: The benchmark models are BERTNLU for natural-language understanding; RuleDST and TRADE for dialogue state tracking; the supervised SL policy; and TemplateNLG and SC-LSTM for natural-language generation. The paper also provides a rule-based user simulator. CITATIONS: ["qasper_2002_11893"]

SUBMIT: A barycentric Newton diagram is a visualization technique that expresses a mixture in terms of its constituents as represented in barycentric coordinates. It draws on Isaac Newton's visualization of the color spectrum and allows an intuitive interpretation of which country a recipe belongs to by mapping probability values from a neural network's activation function. The countries on the Newton diagram are placed by spectral graph drawing so that similar countries are positioned nearby on the circle. CITATIONS: ["qasper_1705_03487"]

SUBMIT: The retrieved abstract and results paragraph say natural-language agents converge faster than the comparison agents, but give no numerical speedup. I cannot quantify how much faster from those passages. CITATIONS: ["qasper_1910_02789"]

SUBMIT: The retrieved passages report LAS and UAS scores for dependency parsing, but do not define how LAS is computed. I cannot supply the definition from this evidence. CITATIONS: ["qasper_1804_05868"]

SUBMIT: The inspected annotation description gives candidate and positive/negative sentiment labels for the debate tweets, but no interannotator-agreement statistic. I cannot report an agreement value from these passages. CITATIONS: ["qasper_1912_05066"]
SUBMIT: The dataset used consists of 4,792 tweets total, a balanced set of 2,396 ironic and 2,396 non-ironic tweets. CITATIONS: ["qasper_1804_08094"]

SUBMIT: The inspected evaluation describes the original metaphor-paraphrase dataset and its contextualized extension, but does not state their language coverage. I cannot confirm that the reported results are English-only from these passages. CITATIONS: ["qasper_1809_01060"]

SUBMIT: Experts labeled the 1,043 sentences of the CoLA development set for 63 minor grammatical features grouped into 15 major features. A sentence receives a major-feature label when at least one of its corresponding minor features is present. CITATIONS: ["qasper_1901_03438"]

SUBMIT: The retrieved passages discuss hardware and training time but provide no measured energy consumption for the NAS run. Hardware counts or runtime alone do not establish energy use, so I cannot give a kWh or joule figure from this evidence. CITATIONS: ["qasper_1901_11117"]
SUBMIT: BoolQ contains about 16,000 questions. CITATIONS: ["qasper_1905_10044"]

SUBMIT: The inspected passages do not specify a maximum number of documents Entity-GCN can handle at once. Counts of candidate entities or graph nodes do not establish a document limit, so I cannot give that figure from this evidence. CITATIONS: ["qasper_1808_09920"]

SUBMIT: The inspected data and experiment passages describe YouTube and Voice Search data but do not specify their language coverage. I cannot identify the training and test languages from this evidence. CITATIONS: ["qasper_2002_11268"]

SUBMIT: The retrieved data description reports 72 million training sentence pairs, and the analysis outline says training-data amount is studied. However, the retrieved analysis/conclusion text gives no numerical comparison across data sizes, so I cannot quantify the impact from that evidence. CITATIONS: ["qasper_1809_04686"]

SUBMIT: When visual attention loses track of the objects, the model still uses that visual information and lets it override the text-based annotations, misleading the translation. CITATIONS: ["qasper_1707_00995"]
SUBMIT: The three datasets are Sexist/Racist (SR), HATE, and HAR. CITATIONS: ["qasper_1809_10644"]
SUBMIT: The paper used a pool of five neural annotator models (DANA models) for dialogue act labeling. CITATIONS: ["qasper_1912_00819"]
SUBMIT: The strong baseline is the RoBERTa-based QA model, which processes each paragraph separately. CITATIONS: ["qasper_2002_09758"]

SUBMIT: The inspected discussion suggests a modular approach combining correction with separate error detection and context handling, and mentions language models for context handling. It does not specify concrete modules for both tasks in these isolated spelling-correction experiments, so I cannot identify a complete proposed solution from these passages. CITATIONS: ["qasper_1905_10810"]
SUBMIT: The experiments use an in-house dataset and the ACE05 dataset. CITATIONS: ["qasper_1911_00069"]
SUBMIT: The two benchmark datasets used are DSTC2 and Maluuba. CITATIONS: ["qasper_1909_09484"]
SUBMIT: They use weGAN to train cross-corpus word embeddings and deGAN to generate document embeddings for multiple corpora. CITATIONS: ["qasper_1712_09127"]
